t: Death Is Not the End; Victory Is
v: Behold, I tell you a mystery. We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
For this perishable body must put on imperishability, and this mortal must put on immortality.
But when this perishable will have put on imperishability, and this mortal will have put on immortality, then what is written will happen: “Death is swallowed up in victory.”
“Death, where is your sting? Hades, where is your victory?”
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
b: Paul lifts our eyes from death to resurrection, and from the present to eternity. Our bodies age and decay and finally face death, but this is not the final end of those who belong to Christ. When the Lord returns, the dead will be raised and those who belong to the Lord will all be changed: “this perishable” will put on imperishability, and “this mortal” will put on immortality. So the Christian’s hope is not only that the soul leaves the world, but that the body is raised, life is made new, and we are with the Lord forever.
From an earthly viewpoint, death looks like the end; from heaven’s viewpoint, death is no longer the last word. The risen Christ is.

How can we be so sure? Because Paul declares: “Thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.” Victory is not our overcoming death by willpower; it is that Jesus has already overcome sin and death through the cross and resurrection. We do not first become victors by our effort and then belong to Christ; because we are united with the victorious Christ, we share in his victory. It is not that I win by myself, but that Christ has already won; it is not that I live, but that the risen Christ lives in me.
So the focus is not on our own ability, nor on the threat of death, but on Jesus, who has risen.

Precisely because the resurrection is real, today’s life has eternal value. Paul does not end by telling believers to sit and wait for the Lord’s return, but says, “Be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work.” The love, faithfulness, service, evangelism, and building up of lives that we give for the Lord today will not be in vain. From a temporary viewpoint, some efforts seem fruitless; from an eternal viewpoint, God remembers every act of faithfulness in Christ. Those who believe in the resurrection do not escape today; they live today more faithfully, because they know that life does not end in death but in resurrection, not in failure but in complete victory in Christ.
a: See Death in the Light of Resurrection
Don’t let death be your final fear; fix your eyes on Jesus, who has risen.
Live in Victory Through the Lord Every Day
Don’t fight in your own strength; live in the victory Christ has already accomplished.
Faithfully Complete the Lord’s Work
Even when you can’t yet see results, stay steadfast and immovable, because your labor in the Lord is never in vain.
q: If I truly believed in the resurrection and in eternity, what should I hold on to, invest in, and faithfully complete today?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. Because Jesus has risen from the dead, I no longer see death as the end of life, but live with eternal hope. Holy Spirit, help me fix my eyes on Jesus every day and let him be King in me, so that I am steadfast and immovable, faithfully completing the work You have entrusted to me. May my whole life be lived in the power of Christ’s resurrection until the day I see the Lord’s face, giving all the glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Thanks be to God, who gives me the victory through my Lord Jesus Christ; my labor in the Lord is not in vain!

t: When You Can’t See a Way, God Is Still Making One
v: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.
The woman conceived, and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.
When she could no longer hide him, she took for him a papyrus basket, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She put the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the river’s bank.
His sister stood far off, to see what would be done to him.
Pharaoh’s daughter came down to bathe at the river. Her maidens walked along by the riverside. She saw the basket among the reeds, and sent her servant to get it.
She opened it, and saw the child, and behold, the baby cried. She had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”
Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Should I go and call a nurse to you from the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?”
Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Go.” The maiden went and called the child’s mother.
Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child away, and nurse him for me, and I will pay you your wages.” The woman took the child, and nursed it.
The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”
b: Moses was born in the most dangerous of times. Pharaoh had ordered that Hebrew baby boys be thrown into the Nile, and Moses’ mother hid him for three months; when she could hide him no longer, all she could do was put the child into a papyrus basket. From a human viewpoint, this was a mother at the point of “nothing more can be done.” But the end of human ability is not the end of God. She did what she could, and then handed over the outcome she could not control. Faith is not doing nothing; it is faithfully doing our part and placing what we cannot control into God’s hands.
Let people be people and God be God; we cannot control tomorrow, but we can trust the God who holds tomorrow.

Even more wonderful, God did not rescue Moses with a dramatic miracle, but worked through a series of seemingly ordinary events: the basket drifted to just the right place, Pharaoh’s daughter came to the river, the baby happened to cry, the princess felt compassion, the sister appeared at just the right moment, and in the end Moses returned to his own mother, and Pharaoh’s daughter even paid the wages for his upbringing. The Pharaoh who wanted to destroy Hebrew baby boys had his own household become the place that protected Moses. When we cannot see God, it does not mean God is not working; many seemingly accidental details may be accomplishing his plan step by step under his sovereignty.

At the time, no one knew that the infant in the basket would one day be the Moses who led Israel out of Egypt. God was not only saving a child; he was preparing the vessel through whom he would later redeem his people. We often see only a small stretch right in front of us, while God sees the whole plan. So don’t let circumstances determine your faith, and don’t lose hope because you can’t yet see a way out. The focus is not whether we can control circumstances, but that God is still in control; we simply follow faithfully and let God lead the next step.
Sometimes we think we are just handing over a “papyrus basket,” while God may be preparing a far greater redemption within it.
a: Do What You Can Do
In difficulty, don’t passively give up; faithfully do the part you can do today.
Entrust What You Can’t Control
Let go of control, let God be God, and believe he is still in charge.
Believe God Is Preparing in Secret
Even if you don’t understand now, don’t lose hope; God’s plan may be bigger than what you see.
q: What is it in my life right now that is beyond my ability, which God wants me to entrust to him after I have faithfully done my part?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, when I cannot see a way out, help me still believe that You are in control. Help me faithfully do what I can do, and humbly let go of outcomes I cannot control. I want to let You be God, let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide each step. Even if I do not yet understand Your arrangements, I believe You are at work, and Your ways are higher than my ways. May my life be wholly in Your hands, accomplishing Your will, so that all the glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will entrust to God what I cannot control, believing he will open a way for me according to his will!

t: Do Not Be Afraid; You Belong to God
v: But now thus says Yahweh who created you, Jacob, and he who formed you, Israel: “Don’t be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your name. You are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they will not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, nor will the flame scorch you.
For I am Yahweh your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
Since you have been precious and honored in my sight, and I have loved you, therefore I will give men in your place, and peoples instead of your life.
Don’t be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your seed from the east, and gather you from the west.
I will tell the north, ‘Give them up!’ and tell the south, ‘Don’t hold them back! Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the end of the earth;
everyone who is called by my name, and whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.’”
b: God said to Israel in her troubles, “Don’t be afraid!” The reason is not that the circumstances have no danger, but that “I have redeemed you… You are mine.” The foundation for overcoming fear is not how much ability I have, but knowing whose I am. Our worth is not determined by people’s opinions, success or failure, or circumstances, but is built on God’s choosing and redeeming us. God says, “I have called you by your name. You are mine.” When we know we belong to God, we no longer need achievements to prove our worth, and we need not grab hold of control of our lives to find security; because we are already in the Lord’s hands.

God did not say that those who belong to him will not pass through waters, rivers, and fire, but said, “I will be with you.” Faith is not a guarantee that life will have no storms; it is a guarantee that in the storms God is present. The water may be deep and the fire may be hot, but circumstances cannot pass beyond God’s sovereignty. God’s greatest promise is not necessarily to lift us out of difficulty at once, but to walk with us in it himself.

So the focus is not how deep the water is or how big the fire is, but how great the God is who walks with us. When we lay down our struggle in our own strength and let Jesus be King, we can have peace even in circumstances we cannot control.

God goes on to say, “You have been precious and honored in my sight, and I have loved you.” And at the end, he says we are those he created “for my glory.” This shows us the whole direction of life: receiving identity from God’s love, walking through life in God’s presence, and in the end living for God’s glory.

We are not here to be king of ourselves or to build our own glory, but to belong to God and live out Christ, so that God receives glory. God redeems us not only to rescue us from trouble, but to make us his own people and to live out the true purpose for which he created us.
a: Remember That You Belong to God
Don’t let people’s opinions and success or failure decide your worth.
Fix Your Eyes on God’s Presence in Water and Fire
Don’t only ask for circumstances to change; believe that God is walking with you.
Live for God’s Glory
No longer centered on yourself; let Jesus be King, so that your life glorifies God.
q: What is the “water” or “fire” that frightens me now? Do I believe that even if circumstances have not yet changed, God is still with me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for redeeming me and calling me, so that I belong to You. As I pass through life’s waters and fires, let my focus be not on myself, not on others, not on circumstances, but fixed on You. I want to lay down my own authority and let Jesus be King in me, believing that Your presence will never leave me. Holy Spirit, guide me to live out the life of Christ and to live all my life for Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not be afraid, for God has redeemed me and called me by name; I am his, and he will be with me!

t: Fan into Flame the Gift God Gave You
v: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, according to the promise of the life which is in Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my beloved child: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers in a pure conscience, how unceasing is my memory of you in my petitions, night and day
For this cause I remind you that you should stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
Therefore don’t be ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner, but endure hardship for the Good News according to the power of God,
who saved us, and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
but has now been revealed by the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus, who abolished death, and brought life and incorruption to light through the Good News.
b: Paul wrote this letter while in prison, and he knew his life was drawing near its end; Timothy was facing a difficult setting for ministry. So Paul reminded him: “Stir up the gift of God which is in you.” The fire is still there; it only needs to be fanned into flame again. Spiritual life can also grow weary from pressure, setbacks, and long years of service, but don’t conclude from a season of low spirits that God no longer uses us. The grace and the commission God gave are still there; what matters is returning to the Lord and letting the Holy Spirit set the fire within us burning again.
Life first, then relationship, then ministry; the fire of service is not kept alive by busyness but is kindled from a real relationship with God.

Paul went on: “God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.” The power God gives is not bravado, the love is not weakness, and the self-control is not timidity. True spiritual strength is to let Jesus remain King under pressure, to hold to the truth in love, and to stay clear-headed in hardship. It is not telling ourselves, “I can definitely do it,” but knowing that God is with me and the Holy Spirit guides me, so I can go forward faithfully.
The focus is not “am I strong enough?” but “is God’s power enough?”; when we no longer rely on ourselves, we can be made strong by the Holy Spirit.

Finally, Paul brought Timothy’s eyes back to the gospel: God saved us and called us, “not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace.” So service is not proving our worth but responding to the grace we have already received. Jesus has also “abolished death” and brought imperishable life to light. We dare to live for the gospel not because we have no weaknesses, but because the risen Christ has already won the victory.

When we set ourselves aside, let Jesus be King, take the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, God can fan us into flame again, so that by his power we complete the mission he has entrusted to us.
a: Fan the Fire of Your Life Again
Return to God’s presence every day, draw near to the Lord again in prayer and Bible reading, and be renewed by the Holy Spirit.
Refuse Timidity; Be Strong in the Lord
In difficulty, don’t look at your own limits, but look to God’s power.
Live for Grace
Don’t serve to prove yourself, but faithfully fulfill God’s commission because you have been shown grace and called.
q: Which gift, prompting, or commission that God placed in my life do I need to “fan into flame” again today?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for saving me and calling me with a holy calling. Please fan again the fire of spiritual life within me, so that I am not fearful because of difficult circumstances, and do not serve in my own strength. I want to let Jesus be King; fill me, Holy Spirit, so that I have a spirit of power, love, and self-control, and faithfully complete the mission You have entrusted to me. May my life reveal Christ, and all the glory go to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: What God has given me is not a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control!

t: In Trouble, Look to God with Undivided Heart
v: (A Prayer by David.) Bow down your ear, Yahweh, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
Preserve my soul, for I am godly. You, my God, save your servant who trusts in you.
Be merciful to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
Bring joy to the soul of your servant, for to you, Lord, do I lift up my soul.
For you, Lord, are good, and ready to forgive, abundant in loving kindness to all who call on you.
Give ear, Yahweh, to my prayer. Listen to the voice of my petitions.
In the day of my trouble I will call on you, for you will answer me.
There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, nor are there any deeds like your deeds.
All nations you have made will come and worship before you, Lord. They will glorify your name.
For you are great, and do wondrous things. You are God alone.
Teach me your way, Yahweh. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name.
I will praise you, Lord my God, with my whole heart. I will glorify your name forevermore.
b: David frankly admitted, “I am poor and needy.” True faith is not pretending to have no needs, but knowing, in our limits, whom to ask for help. David did not let trouble push him away from God; instead he said, “In the day of my trouble I will call on you, for you will answer me.” Difficulty can make a person rely more on themselves, or rely more deeply on God; the key is where we place our focus.
When the focus turns from the problem to God, and from our own ability to God’s ability, trouble can become a place of deeper experience of God.

The foundation of David’s prayer was not his own qualifications but God’s nature: “You, Lord, are good, and ready to forgive, abundant in loving kindness.” We dare to come before God not because we are good enough, but because God is good. When we look only at ourselves, we easily become either proud or discouraged; when we fix our eyes on God, we see his loving kindness, faithfulness, and grace. True peace is not believing “I can definitely handle this,” but believing “God is still in control.”
Let people be people and God be God; admitting our limits is just the beginning of experiencing God’s limitless grace.

Most precious of all, David asked God not only to resolve his trouble but to “teach me your way; I will walk in your truth; make my heart undivided to fear your name.” This shows that mature prayer is not only “Lord, change my circumstances,” but “Lord, change me in my circumstances.” With the Bible as our standard, let God’s truth correct our path; to fear God with an undivided heart is to no longer let the heart be pulled by self, others, and circumstances, but to put God first and let him be King. The greatest blessing of trouble is not only that the problem is solved, but that in it we come to know God more, obey God more, and become more like Christ.
a: Call on God First in Trouble
Don’t let worry be your first reaction; let prayer be your first reaction.
Correct Yourself with the Truth
Don’t only ask God to do things your way; ask him to teach you to walk in his way.
Fear God with an Undivided Heart
Don’t let your heart be pulled away by circumstances; put your focus back on God and let him be King.
q: What weighs on my mind most right now? Is it filling my heart with circumstances, or making me look to God with greater single-heartedness?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, in the day of trouble I will call on You, for You are a good God, abounding in loving kindness. Keep my heart from being pulled away by circumstances, other people, or myself, and help me look to You with an undivided heart. Teach me Your way so that I walk in Your truth; let Jesus be King in me and the Holy Spirit guide my every step. Whatever the circumstances, I will praise You with my whole heart and glorify Your name forevermore. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: In the day of trouble I will call on God, for he will answer me; I will fear his name with an undivided heart!

t: Remember God’s Faithfulness and Proclaim His Salvation
v: Remember his marvelous works that he has done, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
[Combined with the previous verse]
He is Yahweh our God. His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant which he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac,
Confirmed the same to Jacob for a statute, to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
saying, “To you I will give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance;”
When you were but a few men in number, yes, very few, and foreigners in it.
They went about from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no man to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes,
saying, “Don’t touch my anointed ones, and do my prophets no harm.”
Sing to Yahweh, all the earth! Show forth his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised. He also is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but Yahweh made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him. Strength and gladness are in his place.
b: After David brought the ark into Jerusalem, he led the people in worship, and first reminded them: “Remember his marvelous works,” and “Remember his covenant forever.” A very important discipline of spiritual life is not forgetting what God has done.

When people meet new difficulties, they easily see only the problem in front of them and forget how God led them in the past; but when we count our blessings, we find that circumstances keep changing while God’s faithfulness never does. Remembering is not living in the past; it is using God’s past faithfulness to build faith for today.

Back then, Abraham’s descendants were “but a few men in number, very few,” even foreigners merely sojourning in the promised land, yet God had made a covenant with them. This shows us that God’s promise does not depend on how much we have now, but on how faithful he is.

People look at numbers, ability, and conditions; God looks at his own purpose and covenant. When we feel small and limited in ability, we do not need to seize power or prove ourselves; we simply return to our rightful place as human beings, let God be God and let Jesus be King, and faithfully walk the road he shows us. What is truly reliable is not “what I can do,” but “what God has already promised.”

Remembering God’s grace will in the end bring forth testimony: “Show forth his salvation from day to day; declare his glory among the nations.” God gives grace not so that it stops with us, but so that we become channels through which grace flows out. Those who have received grace should bear witness to grace, and those who have received the gospel should proclaim the gospel.

We live not to build our own reputation, but to let all peoples see God’s glory; not “what I have done,” but to testify to “what God has done.” When life turns from self to God, and from receiving to giving, we can build God’s divine order, so that more people come to know Jesus, and all the glory goes to God.
a: Remember God’s Grace Every Day
Recall how God has led, provided for, and kept you, and build faith through thanksgiving.
Believe God’s Promises
Even when your conditions are limited now, believe that God’s faithfulness does not change.
Proclaim God’s Salvation Day After Day
Don’t keep grace to yourself; take the initiative to share what God has done in your life.
q: What wonderful things has God done for me in the past? Which story of grace can I share with someone today?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, help me always remember Your works, and not forget Your faithfulness because of present circumstances. Even though I am small and limited in ability, I still believe that Your promises never change. I want to let Jesus be King; Holy Spirit, guide me so that my life is not for myself but proclaims Your salvation day by day and tells of Your wonders, so that more people come to know You, and all honor, power, and glory go to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will remember God’s covenant forever, proclaim his salvation day after day, and tell of his wonders among all peoples!

t: We Are Blessed So That Others May Be Blessed
v: Now Yahweh said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, to the land that I will show you.
I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.
I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who curses you. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”
So Abram went, as Yahweh had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.

Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all their possessions that they had gathered, and the people whom they had acquired in Haran, and they went to go into the land of Canaan. They entered into the land of Canaan.
Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. The Canaanite was then in the land.
Yahweh appeared to Abram, and said, “I will give this land to your seed.” He built an altar there to Yahweh, who had appeared to him.
He left from there to the mountain on the east of Bethel, and pitched his tent, having Bethel on the west, and Ai on the east. There he built an altar to Yahweh, and called on Yahweh’s name.
b: When God called Abram, he did not first hand him the whole map of his life; he only said, “To the land that I will show you.” Abram had to leave his familiar country, relatives, and father’s house, and walk toward a future not yet fully known. True faith is not obeying only after everything is clear; it is following because we know who is calling us, even when we do not yet know where the next stop is.

We often think we hold the direction, but God wants us to lay down control, and turn from “where do I want to go?” to “Lord, where are you taking me?” When we let God be God and Jesus be King, obedience becomes faith in action.

God said to Abram, “I will bless you… You will be a blessing.” This sentence reveals the true purpose of being blessed. God blesses us not so that the grace stops with us, but so that we become a blessing to others.

The self-centered life asks, “How much more can I get?” The selfless life asks, “How can everything God has given me bless others?” Wealth, ability, gifts, time, experience, and even the road our life has traveled can all become vessels in God’s hands. True abundance is not only that I have a lot, but that God can use me to bring more people to receive his grace.

After Abram reached Canaan, he did something very important: he built an altar and called on Yahweh’s name. It is worth noticing that his life had both a “tent” and an “altar.” The tent showed that he knew he was only a sojourner on earth; the altar showed that God was the true center of his life. Circumstances can change and dwelling places can move, but the place of worshiping God cannot change.

Those who follow God do not build their own kingdom, but wherever they go, they let God be King there. When we take Jesus as our focus, the Bible as our standard, and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we can go from being people who are blessed to being people who make others blessed, so that God’s blessing flows through us to more lives.
a: Obey When You Hear
You needn’t wait until everything is clear; when you know God’s leading, faithfully take the next step.
Be Blessed to Be a Blessing
Use the time, ability, gifts, and resources God gave you to build up others.
Build an Altar Wherever You Go
Whatever changes in your circumstances, put God first and let Jesus be King.
q: What grace has God already given me? How can I use it today so that one person is blessed through me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for calling me and promising to guide my path. Keep me from clinging to my own life plans, and help me follow You in faith. Everything You have given me I place in Your hands, wanting to build nothing for myself, but to be a blessing to others. Let Jesus be King in me, and Holy Spirit, guide my steps, so that wherever I go I worship You and glorify You, and many people receive Your grace through my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God will bless me, and I will make others blessed, so that many are blessed through me!

t: Put Off the Old Self, Live Out the New Self
v: But you did not learn Christ that way;
if indeed you heard him, and were taught in him, even as truth is in Jesus:
that you put away, as concerning your former way of life, the old man, that grows corrupt after the lusts of deceit;
and that you be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
and put on the new man, who in the likeness of God has been created in righteousness and holiness of truth.
b: Paul did not say, “You have learned Christ, so you know more doctrine,” but that we are to “put away the old man and put on the new man.” The Christian faith is not just adding Bible knowledge; it is life truly being changed by Christ. The purpose of learning Christ is not only to know Christ, but to live out Christ.

If we only add information but our lives do not change, the truth remains in our heads; real learning is letting God’s word enter our lives, so that our thoughts, attitudes, choices, and way of living become more and more like Jesus.

Paul points out that the “old man” grows corrupt through the lusts of deceit. The core of the old self is a life that has left God and is centered on self: I want it my way, to satisfy my desires, to protect my interests, even to be my own king. The gospel does not simply tidy up this old self a little; it says to “put away the old man.” Selflessness is not improving myself, but no longer letting the old self be king; it is no longer I, but Christ living in me.
When we return to our rightful place as human beings and lay down our own authority, we can truly let Jesus be King.

The key to life change is in verse 23: “Be renewed in the spirit of your mind.” Change in outward life has its source in a renewed mindset within. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your way of living changes.

When we turn from a human viewpoint to God’s viewpoint, from an earthly viewpoint to a heavenly one, and from the temporary to the eternal, life begins to change. Putting on the new self is not acting out being a better Christian by our own effort, but letting the Holy Spirit renew us through the truth, so that Christ’s new life is lived out from within, revealing God’s righteousness and holiness.
a: Put Off the Old Self Every Day
When you see self-centeredness, pride, and selfish desire, no longer follow the old life.
Renew Your Mindset Every Day
Let the Bible correct your thinking, and learn to see people, events, and yourself from God’s viewpoint.
Put On the New Self Every Day
Let Jesus be King and the Holy Spirit guide, and live out the life of Christ in daily life.
q: Which thought or habit of the old self most needs to be “put off” in my life now? How does God want me to live out the new self in this?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me new life in Christ. Shine Your light on me, that I may see the self-centered, proud, and selfish-desire life of the old self. I am willing to put off the old self and no longer crown myself; renew my mind through the truth, let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide me, so that I put on the new self every day, becoming more and more like Christ, and live out the righteousness and holiness of truth, so that all the glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will put off the old self, be renewed in my mind, and put on the new self created in the likeness of God!

t: Do Not Repay Evil for Evil; Overcome Evil with Good
v: Be of the same mind one toward another. Don’t be conceited, but associate with the humble. Don’t be wise in your own conceits.
Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
Don’t seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to the wrath of God. For it is written, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord.”
Therefore “If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink; for in doing so, you will heap coals of fire on his head.”
Don’t be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
b: Paul teaches us: “Be of the same mind one toward another. Don’t be conceited… Don’t be wise in your own conceits.” Many conflicts between people are often not because the matter is so serious, but because each person wants to insist on being right and wants others to do things their way. Pride makes people contend for the upper hand; humility makes unity possible.

When we are centered on ourselves, we easily look down on others and cling to our own opinions; when we set ourselves aside and let Jesus be King, we can learn to respect, accept, and understand others. True humility is not denying our own worth, but no longer putting ourselves at the center, and being willing to build others up with the love of Christ.

Paul goes on: “Repay no one evil for evil… be at peace with all men.” When someone hurts us, the most natural reaction is to strike back; when someone says an unkind word, we want to answer with a harsher one. The result is pride provoking pride, anger fighting anger, and both sides getting hurt. Repaying evil with evil only makes evil spread; overcoming evil with good is what truly breaks the cycle of hatred.

God says, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay.” This is not telling us to condone sin or give up proper protection, but not to let revenge rule our hearts. Hand the final judgment over to God; let people be people and God be God. We are responsible for doing good according to the truth, and letting God carry out justice.

Finally, Paul gives a life principle that goes beyond human nature: “If your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him a drink.” This is not done by gritting our teeth and enduring, but by letting the life of Christ be lived out from within us. On the cross Jesus did not repay evil with evil; he prayed for those who hurt him. True victory is not defeating the one who hurt me, but not letting his evil change me from living out Christ’s life.

When we set aside our face, our rights, and our desire for revenge, and submit to the Holy Spirit’s guidance, we can replace rage with gentleness, hatred with forgiveness, and cursing with blessing. This is the selfless life, and it is the testimony that Christ is King in us.
a: Replace Pride with Humility
Don’t insist you are always right; learn to respect, understand, and accept others.
Replace Strife with Peace
In conflict, don’t rush to strike back; first seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance and respond with love and truth.
Overcome Evil with Good
Don’t let another’s evil decide your reaction; let go of revenge and hand justice over to God.
q: When others hurt me, misunderstand me, or offend me, am I letting my pride be king, or letting Jesus live out humility, forgiveness, and love in me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for letting me know true love through Jesus Christ. Shine Your light on me, that I may see the pride, anger, and desire for revenge within me. I want to set myself aside, no longer repaying evil with evil, and no longer fighting for my own pride in my own strength. Fill me, Holy Spirit, and let Jesus be King in me, so that I replace pride with humility, rage with gentleness, hatred with forgiveness, and overcome evil with good. May I live at peace with others and live out the life of Christ, so that all the glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not be overcome by evil, but by the Lord’s strength I will overcome evil with good!

t: Who Is King Decides Your Life
v: Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel to Ramah.
They said to him, “Behold, you are old, and your sons don’t walk in your ways. Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”
But the thing displeased Samuel when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.” Samuel prayed to Yahweh.
Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they tell you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me, that I should not be king over them.
According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, in that they have forsaken me and served other gods, so they also do to you.
Now therefore, listen to their voice. However, you shall solemnly warn them, and shall show them the way of the king who shall reign over them.”
b: The elders of Israel asked Samuel to appoint a king for them, and their reason was: “like all the nations.” On the surface, they wanted to solve the problem of leadership succession, because Samuel was old and his sons did not walk in his ways. But God pointed to a deeper problem: “They have not rejected you, but they have rejected me, that I should not be king over them.” The real crisis was not that Israel lacked a king, but that they were unwilling to let God be King.

They envied the systems of the nations and wanted to replace trust in the unseen God with a visible king. We are prone to do the same today. When trouble comes, we reach for human methods, power, and guarantees, forgetting to seek God’s will first. The question is not only which method we choose, but who is deciding the direction of our lives.

When Samuel heard the people’s demand, he was displeased, yet he did not argue with them right away. Instead, he first prayed to Yahweh. This is an important example for life. Another person’s decision may grieve me, but I do not have to let my emotions make my decisions for me.

A self-centered life is easily wounded when rejected and is eager to prove itself right. A humble life is willing to come before God first and seek his heart. Samuel brought the people’s request to God, and God helped him see that the real issue behind it was the people’s rejection of God’s sovereignty. When we stop focusing on how we are being treated and turn instead to God’s will, we can move from emotional reaction to obedient action.

In the end, God told Samuel to listen to the people’s demand, while also warning them how a king would rule over them. This reminds us that God’s allowing people to make a choice does not mean God delights in their choice.

People may insist on their own way, but they must also bear the consequences of their choices. What Israel truly needed was not merely a new political system, but the restoration of God’s kingship in their lives. The same is true for us today. The greatest change in life is not a new environment, method, or system, but a turn from “I want to be king” to “let Jesus be King.” When we take the Bible as our standard, the Holy Spirit as our guide, and Jesus as our example, and let him reign in our lives, we move from building our own system to building God’s divine order, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Do not blindly imitate the world
When facing a choice, do not only look at what others do, but seek God’s will.
Pray first in conflict
Do not let emotions decide your reaction; come before God first and seek his guidance.
Let Jesus be King every day
Lay down your own sovereignty, stop insisting on your own way, and let God’s truth decide the direction of your life.
q: In my life, my family, my relationships, and my service, what things am I still ruling myself, without truly letting Jesus be King?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who created me, redeemed me, and guides me. Please shine Your light on me so that I can see the old self within me that wants to be in charge, to seize power, and to insist on my own way. I am willing to lay myself down, return to my rightful place as a human being, let You be God, and let Jesus be King in me. Holy Spirit, lead me so that I do not blindly imitate the world or make decisions by my own feelings and preferences, but seek Your will in everything, follow Your truth, live out the life of Christ, and build God’s divine order, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not imitate the world or insist on my own way; I will let Jesus be my King and follow God’s will all my life!

t: In Weakness, Experience God’s Perfect Power
v: For if I would desire to boast, I will not be foolish; for I will speak the truth. But I forbear, so that no man may account of me above that which he sees in me, or hears from me.

By reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted excessively, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to torment me, that I should not be exalted excessively.
Concerning this thing, I begged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
He has said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.” Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.
b: Paul received extraordinary revelations, yet he did not exalt himself. Instead, he said that God allowed a thorn to be given to him in the flesh so that he would not be excessively proud. The Bible does not say clearly what the thorn was, but Paul clearly saw one spiritual lesson in it: learning humility. The danger for people is not only weakness, but also pride because of their own strength.

When people have gifts, achievements, and abilities, it is easy to treat the grace God has given as their own talent, and even to try, without realizing it, to take God’s place. Sometimes God allows us to experience our limits so that we stop depending on ourselves and return to our rightful place, letting God be God. Humility is not denying our own worth, but acknowledging that everything is God’s grace and letting Jesus be King in our lives.

Paul asked the Lord three times to take the thorn away, hoping the Lord would remove it. But the Lord did not remove the difficulty as he expected. Instead he answered, “My grace is sufficient for you.” This helps us understand that when God answers prayer, he does not always change the circumstances; sometimes he gives sufficient grace within them.

We often ask God to take away our weakness, but God wants us to learn to depend on him in it. We hope the problem will vanish, but God lets us experience the power of his presence while the problem remains. True faith is not believing that we can overcome every difficulty ourselves, but believing that whatever we face, the Lord’s grace is enough to sustain us in doing his will.

The most wonderful thing is that Paul was no longer ashamed of his weakness. He said, “Most gladly therefore I will rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest on me.” He understood that God’s power is not built on human self-confidence, but is made perfect in human weakness. Selflessness does not mean having no ability; it means no longer depending on our own ability, so that Christ’s power is displayed in me.

When we let go of the stubborn thought “I must do it” and turn to “Lord, may you accomplish it in me,” our life moves from self-centeredness to selflessness, from depending on ourselves to depending on Christ. Weakness is no longer only an obstacle; it can become the place where we experience God’s grace. In the end, what is worth boasting about is not how strong I am, but how great a power Christ displays in me.
a: Learn humility in weakness
Do not be proud of gifts and achievements, and do not be discouraged by your limits; acknowledge that everything is God’s grace.
Depend on grace in difficulty
In prayer, ask not only that God remove the problem, but that he give strength so you can faithfully follow him through it.
Let Christ’s power be displayed
Let go of the habit of depending on yourself, seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance in everything, and let Jesus live in you and be King in you.
q: What weaknesses or difficulties in my life have I kept hoping God would take away? Today, am I willing to learn humility in them and experience the Lord’s sufficient grace?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for helping me understand that Your grace is sufficient for me and that Your power is made perfect in weakness. Please remove the pride within me, so that I no longer depend on my own cleverness, ability, and achievements, and am not discouraged by my weakness. When difficulties do not leave right away, give me faith to experience Your sufficient grace. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me. Let the Holy Spirit lead my life, so that Christ’s power is displayed in me and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: The Lord’s grace is sufficient for me, and his power is made perfect in my weakness!

t: In Christ, Every Heavenly Blessing
v: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ;
even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and without defect before him in love;
having predestined us for adoption as children through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his desire,
to the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he freely gave us favor in the Beloved.
In him we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,
which he made to abound toward us in all wisdom and prudence,
making known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he purposed in him
to an administration of the fullness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens, and the things on the earth, in him;
in whom also we were assigned an inheritance, having been foreordained according to the purpose of him who works all things after the counsel of his will;
to the end that we should be to the praise of his glory, we who had before hoped in Christ.
In him you also, having heard the word of the truth, the Good News of your salvation—in whom, having also believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
who is a pledge of our inheritance, to the redemption of God’s own possession, to the praise of his glory.
b: Paul begins by declaring, “God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ.” This shows us that true blessing is not only wealth, health, achievement, and success on earth, but the eternal grace God has already given us in Christ. Before the foundation of the world, God chose us in Christ, and out of love he adopted us as his children through Jesus Christ. Our most precious identity is not what we own in this world, but whom we belong to in Christ.

The world measures a person’s worth by wealth, position, and achievement, but the gospel lets us know that God loves us and accepts us, making us his children. When our mindset turns from earth to heaven and from the temporary to the eternal, we no longer need to prove our worth by our performance, and we can live truly free lives in God’s love.

Paul goes on to say that “we have our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses,” all according to the riches of God’s grace. The greatest human problem is not a lack of outward blessings, but that sin separates us from God. The greatest blessing is not getting more things, but being restored to a relationship with God through Jesus Christ. The gospel does not merely give us God’s blessings; it gives us God himself.

God redeems us not so that we continue to live for ourselves, but so that we are freed from the grip of the old self and Christ lives in us. God’s eternal purpose is to sum up all things in heaven and on earth in Christ. This reminds us that true unity is not centered on people but on Christ; when we lay ourselves down and let Jesus be King, we can build lives and relationships of unity in him.

Finally, Paul says that when we heard the gospel of salvation and believed in Christ, we were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit, who is also the pledge of our inheritance. This means God not only saves our past and forgives our sins; he also guides us today through the Holy Spirit and gives assurance for our future inheritance. The Father chose us, Christ redeemed us, and the Spirit sealed us; through the grace of the triune God, we are changed from sinners to children of God, from the old life into the new life, from living for ourselves to living for God.

This passage repeats the same purpose again and again: “to the praise of his glory.” So a life that has received grace is not about gaining all the glory for ourselves, but about letting Jesus be King so that God receives all the glory through us.
a: Treasure heavenly blessings
Stop measuring yourself by wealth, position, and achievement, and treasure your identity as God’s child in Christ.
Live out a new life of grace
Remember the redemption of Jesus’ precious blood, let go of self-centeredness, and let Christ live in you.
Obey the Spirit, give glory to God
Seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance every day, let Jesus be King, and make your life a testimony to God’s glory.
q: What do I value most now: wealth, achievement, and blessings on earth, or the salvation, sonship, and eternal inheritance I already have in Christ? Am I truly letting Jesus be King in my life so that God receives glory?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for blessing me in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places. You chose me in love and made me Your child through Jesus Christ; You redeemed me by his precious blood, forgave my trespasses, and gave the Holy Spirit as the pledge of my inheritance. Please renew my mindset so that I am no longer satisfied with earthly wealth and success, but take You as the greatest blessing of my life. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me. Let the Holy Spirit guide me, so that I live out the life of Christ, am united with all the saints in him, follow Your will in everything, and become a praise to the glory of Your grace. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: In Christ I have every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places; redeemed by his blood and sealed by the Holy Spirit, I will live all my life to the praise of God’s glory!

t: Fight in Faith and Receive a Rich Inheritance
v: He gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh a portion among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of Yahweh to Joshua, even Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron. (Arba was the father of Anak.)
Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.
He went up from there against the inhabitants of Debir. (Now the name of Debir before was Kiriath Sepher.)
Caleb said, “He who strikes Kiriath Sepher and takes it, I will give Achsah my daughter as wife.”
Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it. He gave him Achsah his daughter as wife.
It happened, when she came, that she moved him to ask of her father a field. She got off her donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What would you like?”
She said, “Give me a blessing. Since you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” He gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
b: Caleb received Hebron, the inheritance God had promised him long before, but the land was still inhabited by the mighty warriors of the Anakim. God’s promise did not spare Caleb from battle; it became the foundation of his faith to press forward courageously. When the twelve spies scouted Canaan, ten of them were afraid when they saw the giants, but Caleb wholly followed Yahweh. Many years later, his faith had not faded with age, and he still faced the challenge before him with courage. True faith is not failing to see the difficulty, but still believing God’s promise in front of it.

We, too, often shrink back because of hard circumstances and limited ability, but God wants us to learn from Caleb: not to focus on our weakness or the size of our circumstances, but on the faithful God. Victory does not depend on how strong we are, but on the fact that the God we rely on is mighty.

Caleb not only fought courageously himself, but also encouraged the next generation to take up the mission. Othniel accepted the challenge, captured Kiriath Sepher, and became a victor. This shows us that true spiritual legacy is not only leaving an inheritance to the next generation, but passing on a life of faith, courage, and obedience to God.

Caleb did not hold everything in his own hands because of his achievements; he gave the next generation the chance to take part, grow, and win. A life that belongs to God does not seek only its own success, but is willing to help others succeed, so that more people rise up to take up God’s commission. When we let go of self-centeredness, stop treating ministry as our own achievement, and value the nurturing of lives and the building of relationships, one person’s victory can lead to many people’s victory.

After Achsah received land in the South, she knew the land needed springs of water, so she made a request of her father, and Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs. Land is an inheritance, but springs are the supply that lets that inheritance keep bearing fruit. God wants us not only to receive an inheritance but also to have living water, so that our lives stay rich and abundant.

Today we may have knowledge, gifts, resources, and opportunities for service, yet if we lack an intimate relationship with God, we can become like dry land that struggles to bear the fruit of life. Jesus is the source of living water, and the Holy Spirit is our guide in daily life and service. When we pursue not only outward achievement but also long for God’s presence and provision, we can let Christ live and reign within us, so that life keeps flowing and becomes a blessing to others.
a: Face challenges in faith
Do not shrink back because difficulties are great; remember God’s promise and faithfully take the step of obedience.
Raise up the next generation of victors
Do not only complete your own mission; encourage, accompany, and equip others so that faith and life are passed on.
Seek living water every day
Do not only pursue outward inheritance and achievement; draw near to God and let the Holy Spirit keep renewing and supplying your life.
q: What promises and commissions has God already given me that I still dare not press into because I fear the difficulties? Am I seeking only an inheritance while neglecting to draw near to God each day and receive living water?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the faithful, covenant-keeping God who gives rich grace. Please give me faith like Caleb’s, to follow You wholeheartedly, so that I am not afraid because of hard circumstances or shrink back because of my limits. I will lay myself down, let Jesus be King in me, and move forward courageously, led by the Holy Spirit. Make me not only a victor myself, but one who is willing to nurture and equip the next generation, so that more people become victors. And supply me every day with the living water of life, so that I have not only outward blessings but a rich spiritual life, live out Christ, and become a blessing to others, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will follow God wholeheartedly, receive the inheritance he gives in faith, receive his rich supply, and be a victor!

t: Let Go of Dependence and Go with the Lord’s Authority
v: He marveled because of their unbelief. He went around the villages teaching.
He called to himself the twelve, and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
He commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their belt,
but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.
He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.

Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you go out from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Most certainly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
They went out and preached that people should repent.
They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed them.
b: Jesus sent the twelve disciples out to preach, not to act alone, but “two by two,” and he gave them authority over unclean spirits. This shows us that true ministry does not rely on our own ability, but receives the Lord’s sending and depends on the authority he gives.

The disciples did not go out to prove themselves by their own talent; they went to represent Jesus and bring the gospel of God’s Kingdom to people. Going out two by two also reminds us that God’s work is not individual heroism but mutual support and working together in unity. When we let go of self-centeredness, stop arguing over who is more important, and let Jesus be King, we can fulfill the Lord’s commission in unity.

Jesus also told the disciples not to take food, a bag, or money, or extra clothing. This is not teaching all Christians that they need not prepare for their daily needs in any circumstance; it was a special instruction the Lord gave for this particular mission, training the disciples to trust his provision. Faith is not preparing nothing; it is not treating our own preparation as our final reliance.

We often think that the more resources and the better conditions we have, the more certain our ministry is. But Jesus wanted the disciples to understand that what truly gives ministry power is not human money, equipment, or experience, but the Lord’s presence and authority. When we stop clinging to what we have and place our lives in the Lord’s hands, we learn to experience God’s provision even in limited circumstances.

The disciples obeyed Jesus’ sending and went out to preach that people should repent, cast out demons, and heal the sick. Their ministry had a clear center: turning people back to God. Jesus also told them beforehand that in some places people would not receive them or listen; the disciples were to testify faithfully, without forcing anyone to accept. Success in ministry is not that everyone accepts me, but whether I faithfully do the Lord’s will.

We cannot control how others respond, but we can decide whether to obey the Lord. True victory is not building our own name and achievements, but letting Christ’s life be displayed through us, so that people come to know the gospel, lives are changed, and all glory goes to Jesus.
a: Accept the sending; obey the Lord’s leading
Do not stop at learning truth; act courageously and bring the gospel to those in need.
Let go of dependence; trust the Lord’s provision
Use the resources God gives wisely, but do not rely on your own ability; seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance in everything.
Work together in unity; serve faithfully
Do not compete for credit or compare, and do not be discouraged by others’ rejection; seek only to complete the Lord’s commission.
q: In life and ministry, what do I rely on most: my own ability, resources, and experience, or the Lord Jesus who sends me? Am I willing to lay myself down and accept his sending?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for calling and sending me through Jesus Christ, so that I have a share in Your gospel work. Please remove the pride, self-centeredness, and dependence on people within me, so that I understand that all true authority and power come from You. I will lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide my every step. Help me learn to work together in unity with my brothers and sisters, supporting one another, not seeking glory for myself, and not losing heart when I meet rejection. May I faithfully proclaim the gospel and live out the life of Christ, so that more people repent and turn to You, and all glory goes to Jesus. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will obey Jesus’ sending, depend on the authority he gives, and faithfully proclaim the gospel!

t: What God Wants Is Not Sacrifices but Life
v: How shall I come before Yahweh, and bow myself before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
Will Yahweh be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my disobedience, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
The voice of Yahweh calls to the city, and wisdom sees your name: “Listen to the rod, and he who appointed it.
b: The prophet Micah raises an important question: what should a person bring in order to please God? Calves? Thousands of rams? Ten thousands of rivers of oil? Even the firstborn, to make up for one’s own sin? These questions, each heavier than the last, expose a mistaken notion people easily hold: that if they pay a high enough price, they can buy God’s acceptance. But what God truly values is not the quantity of outward offerings, but the real relationship between a person and him. God does not want religious acts to replace a changed life; he wants us to live out his heart in daily life.

Worship, giving, and service are certainly important, but if a life is still full of pride, selfishness, and injustice, no amount of religious activity can replace true repentance and obedience. Life first, then relationships, then ministry; only when life is right do worship and service have real meaning.

God makes plain what he requires: “to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God.” These three show the beauty of a life that belongs to God. To act justly is to treat others according to God’s truth; to love mercy is to treat others with God’s kindness; to walk humbly is to lay down our own sovereignty and let God be God.

Justice keeps us from harming others for our own gain; mercy leads us beyond insisting on right and wrong to understanding and supporting the weak; humility keeps us from exalting ourselves and leads us to obey God’s guidance. Pride makes people leave their rightful place and try to seize authority that belongs to God; humility makes people return to their rightful place and let God reign in their lives. When we take Jesus as our example, the Bible as our standard, and the Holy Spirit as our guide, justice and mercy are no longer merely outward demands but flow naturally from Christ’s life within us.

Most precious of all, God wants not only that we do some right things, but that we “walk with your God.” This means faith is not occasionally coming before God to fulfill a religious duty, but keeping an intimate relationship with God every day, letting him guide our thoughts, words, choices, and actions. Verse 9 also reminds us that God’s call carries a warning of justice, and the truly wise will fear his name and listen carefully to his word. True godliness is not how much I have done for God, but how much God has changed in my life.

When we lay down the old self-centered life, and let Jesus live in us and be King in us, we move from valuing only religious activity to living out Christ every day; from pursuing our own achievements to doing God’s will, so that all glory goes to him.
a: Act justly; live out the truth
In family, work, and relationships, act according to God’s truth, and do not sacrifice others’ rights for your own interests.
Love mercy; treat people with love
Do not only see others’ faults, but also their needs; learn to care for, accept, and support them with Christ’s love.
Walk humbly with God every day
Lay down your own sovereignty, stop insisting on your own way, seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance in everything, and let Jesus be King.
q: Does my faith stay at the level of outward acts of worship, giving, and service, or do I truly live out justice, mercy, and humility, walking with God every day?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for showing me clearly what is good, and for helping me understand that what You delight in is not only outward religious acts but a life that truly obeys You. Please shine Your light on me so that I can see the pride, selfishness, and injustice within me. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide each of my days. Help me act justly according to truth, love mercy with a heart of love, and walk with You in humility. May my life, relationships, and ministry display the life of Christ, so that people come to know Your love and justice through me, and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will act justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with my God every day!

t: True Wealth Is Being a Blessing to Others
v: Charge those who are rich in this present world that they not be arrogant, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who gives us richly all things to enjoy;
that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to share;
laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may take hold of that which is eternal life.
b: Paul reminds those who are rich in this present world: “not to be arrogant, nor to have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches.” Money itself is not sin, and being rich is not the problem; the real danger is becoming proud because of wealth, or treating money as the security of one’s life. Wealth can improve life but cannot become the master of life; money can provide convenience but cannot take God’s place.

If people measure their worth by wealth, they easily become proud when they have it and fearful when they lose it. Paul is not asking the rich to give up enjoying all that God has given, but reminding them that all of it is God’s grace. True humility is acknowledging that we are only stewards entrusted with it, and that God is the owner of everything. When we let go of dependence on wealth and let Jesus be King, we move from a life controlled by money into the freedom of depending on God.

Paul then points out that the rich should not only have wealth but “be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to share.” This shows us that true wealth is not in how much I own, but in how many people are blessed through me.

A self-centered life only wants to accumulate, grasp, and enjoy; a selfless life is willing to share, give, and help others succeed. The money, time, ability, gifts, and resources God gives us are not for building our own kingdom, but for becoming channels of blessing to others. When we turn from “I want to get more” to “I want more people to be blessed,” our life shifts from self-centeredness to Christ-centeredness. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than possessions; money should be used to serve people and build relationships, not to hurt people and damage relationships in pursuit of wealth.

Finally, Paul says that doing so is “laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may take hold of that which is eternal life.” This does not mean people can earn salvation by giving, but reminds us that those who have received grace and been saved should manage their present wealth with an eternal perspective. Earthly wealth is temporary, but life in Christ is eternal; the value of money lies not only in what it can buy, but in what it can accomplish for God’s Kingdom.

When we let Jesus be King, with the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we can use temporary resources for things of eternal value. A truly victorious life is not measured by how much property is left behind, but by faithfully managing all that God has entrusted, living out Christ’s love, and helping more people take hold of true life, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Do not rely on money; rely on God alone
Give thanks for all God has given, and do not let wealth decide your worth, security, or life direction.
Be rich in good works
Willingly share money, time, and resources, and take the initiative to care for those in need, becoming a blessing to others.
Manage wealth with an eternal perspective
Do not only accumulate for this life; faithfully use what God has entrusted to support gospel work, nurture lives, and build God’s divine order.
q: What do I rely on most now: the money in my hands, or the God who richly gives all things? How much of what God has given me has truly become a blessing to others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who richly gives all things and supplies all my needs. Please guard my heart so that I am not proud in abundance or fearful in lack, and so that I do not rely on uncertain riches but on You alone. I am willing to let go of self-centeredness, no longer accumulating only for myself, but sharing gladly and giving willingly, so that more people are blessed through me. Give me heavenly wisdom to faithfully manage all You have entrusted to me and to use this life’s resources with an eternal perspective. May Jesus be King in me and the Holy Spirit guide my life, so that I am rich in good works, take hold of true life, and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I do not rely on uncertain riches but on the God who richly gives all things; I will be rich in good works and take hold of true life!

t: When Trouble Comes, Inquire of God First
v: This is the history of the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham became the father of Isaac.
Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his wife.
Isaac entreated Yahweh for his wife, because she was barren; and Yahweh was entreated by him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
The children struggled together within her. She said, “If it is so, why do I live?” She went to inquire of Yahweh.
Yahweh said to her, “Two nations are in your womb. Two peoples will be separated from your body. The one people will be stronger than the other people. The elder will serve the younger.”
When her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
The first came out red all over, like a hairy garment. They named him Esau.
After that, his brother came out, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel. He was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
b: Isaac married Rebekah at forty, but it was not until he was sixty that he had his twin sons, so there were twenty years of waiting in between. Though Isaac was the son of promise and heir of the covenant with Abraham, he still faced the difficulty of a barren wife. This reminds us that those who receive God’s promises do not necessarily have a life without trouble, and having God with us does not mean everything is accomplished at once.

Isaac did not give up while waiting, nor did he solve the problem only by his own methods; he entreated Yahweh for his wife. God answered his prayer, and Rebekah conceived. True faith is not demanding that God act on our timetable, but continuing to depend on him while we wait. When we let go of our control and let God be God, we can go on trusting his faithfulness even before we see results.

After Rebekah conceived, she found that the children struggled together within her, and she was deeply troubled. She did not stay in her own questions and pain, but “went to inquire of Yahweh.” This is a precious spiritual example. When we meet something we do not understand, we should not first guess with our own minds, but first go before God to seek his heart.

God told her that the two children in her womb would become two nations, and that the elder would serve the younger. This shows that God’s plan is not limited by human tradition and order; he has his own sovereignty and purpose. We often judge things by our own experience, habits, and standards, but God wants us to turn from a human viewpoint to God’s viewpoint, and to see his deeper plan beyond what appears before us. When we take the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we can learn to seek God in circumstances we do not understand, rather than letting our own ideas reign.

At last the twins were born; Esau came out first, and Jacob followed, his hand holding his brother’s heel. This detail foreshadows the complicated relationship between the two brothers. Jacob’s name means “grasping,” and his later life repeatedly showed a tendency to grasp blessings by his own effort. Yet God’s promise is not fulfilled by human scrambling; it comes from God’s grace and faithfulness. People like to grasp what they want by themselves, but faith learns to let go of ourselves and receive what God gives.

Our greatest change is not from lack to abundance, but from depending on ourselves to depending on God, from making ourselves king to letting Jesus be King. When we no longer strive for everything by our own methods but humbly obey God, his will is accomplished in our lives and all glory goes to him.
a: Keep praying while you wait
Do not lose heart because prayer has not yet been answered; learn to trust God’s timing and arrangement.
Inquire of God when confused
Do not rush to judge by your own experience; seek God’s will through prayer and the Bible.
Let go of grasping; learn to entrust
Do not obtain blessings by scrambling and control; let Jesus be King and obey God’s leading.
q: What am I anxiously waiting for now, or trying to secure by my own methods? Am I willing to inquire of God first and hand the sovereignty over to him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the faithful, covenant-keeping God who hears prayer. When I face difficulty, long waiting, or things I do not understand, help me not to lose heart, not to be impatient, and not to depend on my own cleverness and methods. I am willing to learn Isaac’s faith, to keep praying to You, and to learn from Rebekah to inquire of You first in my confusion. Renew my mindset so that I turn from depending on myself to depending on You, from grasping my own way to obeying Your will. May Jesus be King in me and the Holy Spirit guide my every step, so that I walk in Your plan all my life and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will entreat God while I wait, inquire of him in my confusion, and trust his promise and guidance!

t: Give Yourself Up for the Gospel; Run Toward the Goal
v: To the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might gain Jews; to those who are under the law, as under the law, that I might gain those who are under the law;
to those who are without law, as without law, not being without law toward God, but under the law toward Christ, that I might win those who are without law.
To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.
Now I do this for the sake of the Good News, that I may be a joint partaker of it.
Don’t you know that those who run in a race all run, but one receives the prize? Run like that, that you may win.
Every man who strives in the games exercises self-control in all things. Now they do it to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
I therefore run like that, as not uncertainly. I fight like that, as not beating the air,
but I beat my body and bring it into submission, lest by any means, after I have preached to others, I myself should be disqualified.
b: Paul says, “I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.” This is not unprincipled pleasing of others; it is a willingness, without compromising Christ’s truth, to lay down one’s own habits, preferences, and rights so that more people may receive the gospel. True self-denial is not losing the truth, but laying yourself down so that others have the chance to know the truth.

A self-centered life demands that others adapt to me; a selfless life is willing to go toward others, understand them, and serve them. Sharing the gospel is not asking people to become like me first, but letting them come to know Jesus through my life. When we stop being self-centered and center on Jesus instead, we can cross differences with Christ’s love and lead more people to receive salvation.

Paul then uses the picture of a race to remind us to run for the prize. Athletes in the world are willing to pay the price, accept training, and exercise self-control in all things for a perishable crown; since we seek an imperishable crown, we should have an even clearer direction and a firmer resolve. The greatest waste in life is not running too slowly, but running hard in the wrong direction.

We often work hard for earthly achievement, wealth, and reputation, but neglect eternal life and the mission of God’s Kingdom. When we turn from a temporary viewpoint to an eternal viewpoint, our life goal changes: no longer only seeking our own success, but living out Christ and leading people to him. When Jesus is King, life has true direction; when Jesus receives the glory, all our effort has eternal value.

Finally Paul says, “I beat my body and bring it into submission.” This is not earning salvation by mistreating the body, but practicing self-control so that selfish desires and the leanings of the flesh do not rule our daily life. Paul knew well that if a preacher of the gospel does not live out the gospel, the message loses its due witness. True victory is not defeating others, but overcoming the selfish desires and self-centeredness of the old self through Christ.

Bringing the body into submission is not making ourselves king, but being led by the Holy Spirit so that body, mind, and life submit to Christ. Life first, then relationships, then ministry; the gospel must first change us before it can bless others through us. When we no longer live for ourselves but let Christ live in us, we can run all our lives toward the mission God has entrusted, as faithful victors.
a: Willingly give yourself up for the gospel
Lay down your habits, preferences, and rights, and take the initiative to understand and care for different kinds of people, so that more people come to know Jesus.
Run wholeheartedly for eternity
Do not let earthly achievement and enjoyment blur your life’s direction; use your time, ability, and resources for things of eternal value.
Bring the body into submission by the Spirit
