Stop following the old self’s selfish desires and self-centeredness; practice self-control, let Jesus be King, and live out the witness of the gospel.
q: What goal am I running toward in life right now? Am I willing to lay myself down for the gospel and, by the Holy Spirit, bring my body into submission, so that more people come to know Jesus through my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me salvation through Jesus Christ and entrusting me with the mission of proclaiming the gospel. Please remove the self-centeredness within me, so that I am willing to lay down my own preferences and rights for the gospel, and understand, care for, and serve others with Christ’s love. Renew my mindset so that I no longer chase a fleeting earthly crown but run the heavenly race with an eternal perspective. I will lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide me and help me bring my body into submission, live out the life of Christ, and faithfully complete the mission You have entrusted, so that more people receive the blessing of the gospel and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will give myself up for the gospel, exercise self-control in all things, run with a clear direction, and receive the imperishable crown!

t: From Weeping and Searching to Seeing the Lord
v: But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So, as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,
and she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
They said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping?” She said to them, “Because they have taken away my Lord, and I don’t know where they have laid him.”
When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, and didn’t know that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?” She, supposing him to be the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.”
Jesus said to her, “Mary.” She turned and said to him, “Rabboni!” (which is to say, “Teacher!”)
Jesus said to her, “Don’t touch me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers, and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”
Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had said these things to her.
b: Mary Magdalene stood weeping outside the empty tomb, because she thought someone had taken Jesus’ body away. She loved Jesus deeply, but because of her grief she did not recognize the risen Lord standing right in front of her. Sometimes it is not that the Lord is not with us, but that our vision is covered by tears and circumstances.

Mary kept looking for Jesus, yet still understood everything before her through the viewpoint of death, not knowing that the risen Lord had already conquered death. We, too, often see only what has been lost because of difficulty, loss, and sorrow, and fail to see what God is accomplishing. When we shift our focus from circumstances to Jesus, and from an earthly viewpoint to a heavenly one, we can see hope again in our tears. True faith is not the absence of sorrow, but still turning in sorrow toward the Lord who lives forever.

The most moving moment is when Jesus himself called, “Mary.” When the Lord called her by name, she recognized Jesus at once and answered, “Rabboni!” What turned Mary from sorrow to joy was not a change in circumstances, but recognizing the risen Lord. Real transformation of life is not only knowing that Jesus rose, but knowing this risen Lord personally.

Jesus did not leave Mary because of her tears; he took the initiative to seek her and call her. This shows us that the Christian faith is not just religious knowledge but a real, intimate life relationship with Jesus. When we quietly listen to the Lord’s voice and let his truth renew our mindset, we can turn from relying on our own judgment to trusting him, from being ruled by sorrow to letting Jesus be King, and his resurrection life can be lived out in us.

Jesus did not let Mary remain in the joy of reunion with him; he sent her to tell the disciples. Mary obeyed the Lord’s word and declared, “I have seen the Lord.” This sentence became her most powerful testimony. Truly meeting the risen Lord not only brings comfort to ourselves, but makes us people who proclaim the gospel.

Mary went from a woman weeping outside the tomb to one who told the disciples the good news of the resurrection; from one who searched for the Lord to one who bore witness to the Lord. God wants to change not only our feelings but our lives, so that we can bless others. When we let Jesus be King, with the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we turn from our own needs to the Lord’s commission, no longer living only for ourselves but living out Christ and proclaiming Christ, so that more people come to know the risen Lord and all glory goes to him.
a: Look to Jesus through your tears
Do not let difficulty and sorrow cover your spiritual vision; believe the risen Lord is still with you.
Draw near to the risen Lord every day
Do not stop at Bible knowledge; build an intimate life relationship with Jesus through truth and prayer.
Share your encounter with the Lord
Do not only receive comfort and hope yourself; witness to others about Jesus so that more people receive the blessing of the gospel.
q: Because of sorrow, difficulty, or loss, am I seeing only my circumstances and overlooking that the risen Lord is with me? Am I willing to share my personal experience of the Lord with others?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for raising Jesus Christ from the dead and giving me eternal life and hope. When I face difficulty, sorrow, and loss, open my spiritual eyes so that I no longer look only at circumstances but fix my eyes on the risen Lord. Help me draw near to Jesus every day and listen to his voice, and let him be King in me and the Holy Spirit guide my life. May I not only experience Your comfort and grace myself, but also boldly witness to Your resurrection and live out the life of Christ, so that more people come to know You through me and receive eternal hope, and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I have seen the Lord! I will fix my eyes on the risen Jesus and boldly proclaim his gospel!

t: Entrust Small Things to God, Experience Great Grace
v: The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “See now, the place where we dwell before you is too small for us.
Please let us go to the Jordan, and every man take a beam from there, and let us make a place there, where we may dwell.” He answered, “Go.”
One said, “Please be pleased to go with your servants.” He answered, “I will go.”
So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they cut down wood.
But as one was felling a beam, the axe head fell into the water. He cried, and said, “Alas, my master! For it was borrowed.”
The man of God said, “Where did it fall?” He showed him the place. He cut down a stick, and threw it in there, and made the iron float.
He said, “Take it up for yourself.” So he put out his hand, and took it.
b: Because the place where they lived was too small, the sons of the prophets decided to go to the Jordan together to cut timber and build a larger dwelling. They not only presented their plan to Elisha, but invited him to go with them. This shows us that God’s work needs not only a good plan, but, more importantly, seeking God’s presence and guidance.

When people see a need, they often rush to meet it with their own experience, ability, and methods, forgetting to seek God first. The sons of the prophets valued not only building a house but also walking together with their spiritual leader. Whether we face family, work, or ministry today, we should learn to seek God’s will first, taking the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide. True building is not only getting things done well but letting God reign throughout the process.

Just as everyone was working hard to cut down trees, one disciple’s axe head suddenly fell into the river. He cried out at once, “Alas, my master! For it was borrowed.” To others it might have been a trivial matter, but to this disciple it was a loss he could hardly bear, because the axe was not his own. Elisha did not blame him for being careless, nor did he belittle his difficulty; he asked, “Where did it fall?” God cares not only about the big events of our lives but also about the small things.

We often think only major crises call for prayer and that small daily difficulties should be handled on our own. But a life that truly depends on God is willing to bring everything, big or small, before him. When we acknowledge our limits and let go of the habit of relying on ourselves for everything, we can experience God’s grace more deeply in daily life.

Elisha cut a stick, threw it into the water, and the axe head floated up. This was a wonderful work God did through the prophet, showing that his power is not limited by natural conditions. Yet Elisha did not pick the axe head up for the disciple; he said to him, “Take it up for yourself.” The man put out his hand and took it. When God shows grace, people also respond in faith and take obedient action.

This miracle was not only the recovery of a lost axe head; it let the disciple know God’s power and care. Today we should not treat a miracle as the solution that must appear in every difficulty, but we can be sure that nothing is too small to bring to God in prayer. When we let Jesus be King and obey his leading in faith, we learn to know God through every experience in life, depend on him more, and give all glory to him.
a: Seek God before you act
Do not rely only on your own plans and abilities; seek God’s will and guidance first in everything.
Pray about big and small things
Do not despise small difficulties in life, and do not lose heart over your limits; learn to entrust everything to God.
Obey and act when you receive grace
Do not only wait for God to change circumstances; in faith, do your part and faithfully respond to God’s leading.
q: In my life and ministry, what things do I habitually handle on my own without bringing them to God? Am I willing to start learning to let Jesus be King from every small matter?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are a God of great power and full of love, who cares not only about the big events of my life but also watches over every small thing in my daily life. Please change my habit of depending on myself in everything, so that I no longer act by my own cleverness and ability but seek Your will first. I am willing to lay myself down, let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide my every step. When I face difficulty, give me faith, so that I learn to entrust, obey, and act. May I experience Your grace in my daily life and live out the life of Christ, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will depend on God in everything, obey his guidance in faith, and experience his grace in big and small matters!

t: Do Not Repay Evil with Evil; Overcome Harm with Blessing
v: Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tender hearted, courteous,
not rendering evil for evil, or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that to this you were called, that you may inherit a blessing.
For, “He who would love life and see good days, let him keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.
Let him turn away from evil, and do good. Let him seek peace, and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears open to their prayer; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”
b: Peter exhorts believers: “Be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tender hearted, courteous.” This shows us that a true spiritual life is expressed not only in our personal relationship with God but also in how we treat the people around us. Unity does not demand that everyone be like me; it means being willing to lay myself down and learn to love one another with the heart of Christ.

Pride makes people insist on their own opinions and compete with one another; humility makes people respect, understand, and build up others. A self-centered life always wants to prove itself right, while a selfless life is willing to let Jesus be King and build relationships with his love. People matter more than tasks, and relationships matter more than possessions; when we no longer hurt people over matters, or damage relationships for gain, we can live out Christ’s life and make the church a spiritual family that loves one another and is united.

Peter goes on: “not rendering evil for evil, or insult for insult; but instead blessing.” This is a teaching that goes against human instinct yet displays the life of Christ. When others hurt us, the old self’s reaction is to strike back at once and make them pay; but God calls us not to answer evil with the same evil, but to break the cycle of harm with blessing. True victory is not making the one who hurt me get hurt, but not letting another’s evil rule my life.

On the cross, Jesus did not return insult for insult but prayed for those who hurt him. Blessing is not approving wrong, nor condoning harm, but not letting hatred replace Christ’s love. When we lay down the right to revenge and let the Holy Spirit guide our response, we can overcome pride with humility and evil with goodness, so that people see Jesus in us.

Finally, Peter reminds us to keep our tongues from evil, turn away from evil, do good, and seek peace and pursue it. This helps us understand that true blessing is not only saying good words, but letting our life, words, and actions all live out God’s goodness.

Words can build people up and can hurt them; one humble, gentle word may resolve a long conflict, while one proud, angry word may destroy a precious relationship. God wants us not only to stop speaking evil but also to actively pursue peace. This is not suppressing our emotions by ourselves, but letting God’s truth renew our mindset and the Holy Spirit change our life, so that Christ’s love flows naturally from the heart. The eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer. When we follow Jesus wholeheartedly and live out humility, compassion, and blessing, we become people who bring blessing to others, and all glory goes to God.
a: Build unity with humility
Do not insist on your own opinions and interests; learn to be considerate, respectful, and accepting, and build relationships of mutual love.
Bless instead of taking revenge
When harmed or offended, do not repay evil for evil or insult for insult; respond in love, relying on the Holy Spirit.
Guard your words; pursue peace
Do not speak words that hurt; take the initiative to do good and resolve conflict, and let your words and actions be a blessing to others.
q: When others offend me, hurt me, or disagree with me, do I let my pride and emotions be king, or do I let Jesus live out humility, compassion, and blessing in me?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving me rich grace in Christ and for calling me to be a blessing to others. Please remove the pride, self-centeredness, and desire for revenge within me, so that I no longer repay evil with evil or hurt others with my words. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide my thoughts, words, and actions. Give me humility, compassion, and love, so that I can understand others, forgive others, and bless others, taking the initiative to seek peace and build relationships of unity. May I live out the life of Christ every day and become a person who brings blessing to others, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will not repay evil with evil but will bless; I will turn from evil and do good, seek peace, and pursue it!

t: Honor God with Your Wealth; Accept Discipline with Humility
v: It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your bones.
Honor Yahweh with your substance, and with the first fruits of all your increase;
so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his correction;
for whom Yahweh loves, he corrects, even as a father corrects the son in whom he delights.
b: Proverbs tells us: “Honor Yahweh with your substance, and with the first fruits of all your increase.” The first fruits are the first part of the harvest, representing a person’s willingness to put God first in life. True giving is not only offering possessions to God but acknowledging that everything belongs to God and letting God be King in life.

A self-centered life thinks wealth is earned by its own effort and so grips it tightly; a selfless life understands that ability, opportunity, health, and resources are all God’s grace, and that we are only stewards entrusted with them. What God values is not only how much we give, but whether we honor him with gratitude, trust, and obedience. When we turn from “this is mine” to “everything is God’s,” we can let go of our grip on possessions and let Jesus truly be King in our life and our money management.

God then promises: “so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.” This is wisdom literature’s picture of the blessing on a life that fears and honors God; it is not a guarantee that everyone who gives will immediately receive more wealth. True abundance is not only having more, but, because God is the Lord of life, knowing how to use well all that he gives.

If people center on wealth, they may still fear losing it even when they have a great deal; but those who center on God can give thanks in abundance, trust in lack, and learn to share in receiving. Giving is not trading with God for blessing; it is an expression of a life that loves and fears God. When we no longer accumulate only for ourselves but are willing to be a blessing to others, God’s grace flows through us to more people, and possessions become tools for serving God, building relationships, and blessing lives.

Finally, Proverbs reminds us: “don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his correction.” God expresses his love not only through provision but also through discipline that helps us grow. A truly loving Father gives us not only what we want but shapes us into people he delights in.

The old self does not like to be corrected, because pride makes us insist we are right; but the humble are willing to accept reminders and let God’s truth correct their mindset and life. God’s discipline is not meant to destroy us but to turn us from mistakes and onto the path of life. When we lay down self-centeredness and are willing to accept God’s correction, we turn from pride to humility, from self-centeredness to selflessness, and let Christ’s life grow in us, living out the holiness and righteousness that God delights in.
a: Put God first in your wealth
Give with gratitude and reverence, acknowledging that everything is God’s grace, and let Jesus be King in your financial management.
Live abundantly with contentment and sharing
Do not measure blessing by how much wealth you have; learn contentment, manage resources faithfully, and willingly be a blessing to others.
Accept discipline with a humble heart
When reminded or rebuked, do not hurry to defend or resist, but examine yourself and let God’s truth renew your life.
q: Do I truly put God first in money, daily life, and life choices? When God reminds or disciplines me through truth or circumstances, do I accept it humbly or resist it proudly?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are a God who gives grace richly and is full of love. You have given me life, ability, and everything I need to live; please help me no longer treat possessions as my security, but honor You with a grateful heart and faithfully manage all You have entrusted to me. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, so that I do not covet wealth but gladly share and become a blessing to others. When You discipline and remind me, remove my pride so that I humbly accept Your correction, and let the Holy Spirit guide me, renewing my mindset, life, and daily living through truth, so that I become more and more like Christ and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will honor Yahweh with my wealth, accept his discipline with humility, and live in the Father’s rich love!

t: Follow Christ’s Humility; Let Jesus Be King
v: Let nothing be done through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus:
who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.
And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to death, yes, the death of the cross.
Therefore God also highly exalted him, and gave to him the name which is above every name;
that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those who are in heaven, those on earth, and those under the earth,
and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
b: Paul exhorts believers: “Let nothing be done through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself.” Many conflicts between people are not that serious in themselves; they come from wanting to compete for status, power, and face, and to be affirmed by others. Pride makes people exalt themselves; humility makes people value others.

A self-centered life centers everything on itself, concerned with its own interests, feelings, and glory; a selfless life is willing to lay itself down and look not only to its own things but also to the things of others. True humility is not denying our own worth but no longer putting ourselves at the center, and being willing to respect, understand, and fulfill others. When we lay down pride and let Jesus be King, we move from rivalry to unity, from self-centeredness to loving one another, and our lives and relationships display Christ’s beauty.

Paul then points to the most perfect example of humility, Jesus Christ. He was in the form of God, yet did not cling to the honor that was rightfully his; he emptied himself, took the form of a servant, was made in the likeness of men, and was even obedient to death on a cross. Jesus’ humility did not mean losing his divinity; it was a willingness to lay down his honor, serve people as a servant, and give his life to save sinners.

This is the most perfect example of self-denial. Out of pride, people want to rise, hold power, and gain glory; but out of love, Jesus willingly came down, served, and sacrificed. He did not prove himself by seizing power, but accomplished the Father’s will through complete obedience. When we have the mind of Christ Jesus, we no longer insist on our rights and interests, but let his humility and love be lived out in us.

Finally, Paul declares that God highly exalted Jesus, so that every knee will bow at his name and every tongue confess that “Jesus Christ is Lord,” to the glory of God the Father. This shows us that the human way is to exalt oneself in pride, while Christ’s way is humble obedience and glory to God.

Jesus accomplished salvation through the cross, and the Father gave him the highest honor. As we follow Christ today, we do not seek to be exalted ourselves but are willing to lay ourselves down and let Jesus live in us and be King in us. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your daily living changes. When we turn from “I am everything” to “the Lord is everything,” from self-centeredness to selflessness, we can live out Christ’s humble, obedient life, build relationships of unity, and faithfully complete what God has entrusted, so that all glory goes to God the Father.
a: Lay down pride; be humble in mind
Do not compete for status, power, and face; learn to respect, understand, and fulfill others.
Follow Jesus; give yourself up willingly
Look not only to your own things but also to the things of others, and serve those around you with a servant’s heart.
Let Jesus be King; give glory to God
Stop exalting yourself, obey God’s will in everything, and let Christ’s life be lived out from within.
q: In my family, relationships, and ministry, am I still trying to win my own status, rights, and glory? In which matter am I willing to follow Jesus’ humility, lay myself down, and let him be King?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for giving Jesus Christ, so that I can see the most perfect example of humility, self-denial, and obedience. Please shine Your light on me so that I can see the pride, self-centeredness, and desire for empty glory within me. I am willing to lay myself down, no longer compete for status, power, and face, but have the mind of Christ Jesus and learn to be humble, considerate, and to fulfill others. Holy Spirit, lead me so that Jesus lives in me and is King in me, so that I look not only to my own things but also to the things of others, serve in love, and follow Your will in obedience. May my life become more and more like Christ, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will have the mind of Christ Jesus, be humble and give myself up willingly, and let Jesus be King, to the glory of God the Father!

t: Ask for Wisdom in Faith; Rely on God Wholeheartedly
v: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven by the wind and tossed.
For let that man not think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
b: James tells us: “If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach.” Life is full of choices, difficulties, and challenges; we often know what we want, but not necessarily what pleases God. True wisdom is not only knowing how to solve a problem but knowing how to act according to God’s will.

Human cleverness values methods, efficiency, and results, while God’s wisdom values truth, life, and eternal worth. God does not blame us for lacking wisdom; he invites us to come humbly before him and ask. When we acknowledge our limits and no longer rely on our own cleverness, but take the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we turn from a human viewpoint to God’s viewpoint and learn to let Jesus be King in our lives.

James goes on: “But let him ask in faith, without any doubting.” He compares the doubter to a wave of the sea driven by the wind and tossed. The doubt here does not mean occasional questions in difficulty, but a wavering heart that wants to rely on God on one hand and is unwilling to trust him fully on the other. Faith is not believing that God will certainly do things my way, but believing that God’s wisdom is higher than mine and being willing to obey his leading.

When we believe only in the results we can see, we easily rise and fall with circumstances, full of faith when things go smoothly and beginning to doubt in hardship. But when we fix our focus on Jesus, we no longer let circumstances decide our faith; God’s truth steadies our hearts so that we can stand firm even in the storm.

Finally, James points out: “A double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.” To be double-minded is to have two directions in the heart: wanting to do God’s will and also wanting to hold on to my own; wanting God to be King and also unwilling to give up my sovereignty. A life cannot have two kings; true faith is laying down myself and wholeheartedly letting Jesus be King.

A self-centered life takes its own preferences and interests as the standard; a selfless life is willing to let God’s truth decide the direction of life. Change your mindset and your life changes; change your life and your daily living changes. When we are no longer double-minded but wholeheartedly seek God, trust God, and obey God, we move from wavering to steadfastness, from depending on ourselves to depending on Christ, and live a life of direction, conviction, and glory to God.
a: Ask God when you lack wisdom
In difficulty and choices, do not hurry to solve things your own way; pray first and seek God’s truth and guidance.
Rely on God wholeheartedly in faith
Do not let changing circumstances shake your faith; believe God’s wisdom is higher than yours and be willing to obey his arrangements.
Be double-minded no more
Lay down your own sovereignty, do not waver between God’s will and your own, and let Jesus be King.
q: In the difficulties and choices I now face, am I truly seeking God’s wisdom in faith, or praying for guidance with one mouth while insisting on my own way, unwilling to let Jesus be King?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who gives wisdom liberally and is full of grace. When I face difficulty, challenges, and life choices, please keep me from relying on my own cleverness and help me come humbly before You to seek Your wisdom. Remove the doubt and double-mindedness within me, so that I am no longer driven by circumstances and emotions but wholeheartedly rely on You in faith. I am willing to lay down my own sovereignty and let Jesus be King in me, and let the Holy Spirit guide my thoughts, choices, and actions. Renew my mindset through truth so that I understand Your will, obey Your leading, and walk all my life on the path that pleases You, and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will ask God for wisdom in faith, be double-minded no more, and rely wholeheartedly on his guidance!

t: The Fear of the Lord Is the Beginning of Wisdom
v: Praise Yah! I will give thanks to Yahweh with my whole heart, in the council of the upright, and in the congregation.
Yahweh’s works are great, pondered by all those who delight in them.
His work is honor and majesty. His righteousness endures forever.
He has made his wonderful works to be remembered. Yahweh is gracious and merciful.
He has given food to those who fear him. He always remembers his covenant.
He has shown his people the power of his works, in giving them the heritage of the nations.
The works of his hands are truth and justice. All his precepts are sure.
They stand fast forever and ever. They are done in truth and uprightness.
He has sent redemption to his people. He has ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awesome.
The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom. All those who do his commandments have a good understanding. His praise endures forever.
b: The psalmist begins by declaring, “Praise Yah!” and says, “I will give thanks to Yahweh with my whole heart.” True praise is not only singing with the mouth, but knowing, remembering, and thanking God from the heart. The psalmist reminds us that Yahweh’s works are great, and what he does is full of honor, majesty, righteousness, grace, and mercy. True worship does not focus on our own needs but turns our focus to who God is and what he has done.

People often remember only the difficulties they meet, forgetting the grace God has already shown; they see only what they still lack and overlook all they have received. When we turn from our own viewpoint to God’s viewpoint, and from complaining to thanksgiving, our life begins to change. Praise keeps us from centering on ourselves and puts God first, giving all glory to him.

The psalmist then points out that God’s works are truth and justice, his precepts are sure, and they stand fast forever and ever. This shows us that God’s word is not merely advice for life but the standard by which we measure all thoughts, values, and actions.

The world’s ideas keep changing, and human standards shift with circumstances, interests, and feelings, but God’s truth stands firm forever. Our greatest problem is not lack of information but that we often judge right and wrong by our own ideas, even wishing God’s word would match our own wishes. True wisdom is laying down our pride and acknowledging that God’s truth is higher than human thinking. When we take the Bible as our standard, let the Holy Spirit lead, and no longer insist on being king ourselves, we turn from human wisdom to God’s wisdom, from a self-centered life to a selfless life in which Christ lives.

Finally the psalmist declares, “The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom. All those who do his commandments have a good understanding.” Fearing God is not staying away from him out of dread, but, because we know his holiness, greatness, and love, willingly honoring him as great and obeying his will. True wisdom is not only knowing God’s word but being willing to do it; true fear of God is letting God be God and letting people be people.

Pride makes people leave their rightful place and try to seize sovereignty and decide everything; humility makes people lay down power, return to the place of the created, and let Jesus be King in life. When we not only hear the word but are willing to do it, God’s truth moves from mindset into life, from life changing daily living, and then influences relationships and ministry. Such a life is truly wise, and it makes God’s name receive everlasting praise.
a: Give thanks wholeheartedly; remember God’s grace
Do not look only at present difficulties; count God’s past works and respond to him with thanksgiving and praise every day.
Take the Bible’s truth as your life’s standard
Do not let your preferences and the world’s ideas decide right and wrong; let God’s word renew your thinking and guide your actions.
Obey God’s word with reverence
Lay down pride and self-centeredness, let Jesus be King, and live out the truth you understand in your daily life.
q: Does my knowledge of God stay at Bible knowledge and verbal praise, or do I truly fear him and let his word change my mindset, life, and daily living?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are a God full of honor, majesty, righteousness, grace, and mercy. The wonders You have done are worth remembering forever, Your truth stands firm forever, and Your faithfulness lasts through all generations. Please remove the pride and self-centeredness within me, so that I no longer rely on my own cleverness but seek You and obey You with reverence. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, let the Bible be my standard, and let the Holy Spirit guide each of my days. Help me not only understand truth but live it, so that my life, daily living, relationships, and ministry all display the beauty of Christ, and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will give thanks to Yahweh with my whole heart, obey his commandments with reverence, and live out true wisdom!

t: Fear God’s Power; Trust God’s Sovereignty
v: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.
Hear attentively the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.
He sends it out under the whole heaven, his lightning to the ends of the earth.
After it, a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back the lightnings when his voice is heard.
God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.
For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth;’ likewise to the shower, and to the great rain.
He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.
Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.
Out of its chamber comes the storm, and cold out of the north.
By the breath of God, ice is given, and the width of the waters is frozen.
Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.
It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,
whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.”
b: Through the thunder, lightning, wind, snow, and rain, Elihu tells Job of God’s great power in creating and governing all things. He says, “God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.” The grandeur and majesty of nature make us see how small we are and remind us that God’s wisdom far exceeds human understanding. True fear of God is not that we know everything God does, but that even when many things cannot be fathomed, we acknowledge that God is still the Lord who reigns.

People often want to figure out every cause and control every outcome, and even want God to act as they think best. But when we see God’s greatness, we realize how limited human wisdom and ability are. Humility is laying down our own sovereignty, returning to our rightful place, and letting God be God. When we no longer center on ourselves but fix our eyes on God, we can trust him even in circumstances we cannot understand.

Elihu goes on to say that God says to the snow, “Fall on the earth,” and likewise to the shower and the great rain; he even seals up the hand of every man so that all may know his work. This shows us that people can work hard but cannot govern everything; they can make plans but cannot decide every outcome.

We are used to proving our ability by being busy and think everything is in our grasp, but sometimes one storm can bring all our arrangements to a halt. God allows us to experience our limits, reminding us that the true security of life is not our own ability but his grace. When we are willing to stop and seek God’s will again, we turn from depending on ourselves to depending on him. True rest is not that everything goes according to plan, but that when plans are disrupted, we still let Jesus be King and trust that God’s wisdom is higher than ours.

Finally, Elihu points out that God moves the clouds and sends the rain, “whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness.” The same wind and rain can bring different results in different situations, reminding us not to judge God’s heart only by present circumstances. We cannot fathom all God’s works, but we can trust his wisdom and sovereignty with reverence.

People easily take smooth times as blessing and hard times as misfortune, but God can use different circumstances to teach us and mature our lives. This does not mean every disaster is God’s punishment, but reminds us to seek him with a humble heart and not to judge others’ circumstances rashly. When we let the Bible renew our mindset and the Holy Spirit guide our life, we turn from a human perspective to God’s perspective, giving thanks in good times and trusting in hard times, honoring the Lord as great in everything, and all glory goes to him.
a: Know God’s greatness; learn humility
Do not be proud of your knowledge, ability, and achievements; acknowledge that God’s wisdom far exceeds human understanding.
Let go of control; trust God’s sovereignty
When plans are blocked or circumstances suddenly change, do not rush to complain; quietly seek God’s leading.
Fear God in every circumstance
Give thanks not only when things are smooth but also trust God in hardship; let Jesus be King and learn to obey his will.
q: When things do not go according to my plan, or I meet difficulties I cannot understand, do I rush to control everything, or am I willing to humbly acknowledge my limits, let God be God, and let Jesus be King?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who created heaven and earth, governs all things, and is full of power. Your wisdom is unfathomable and Your works are wonderful and awesome. Please remove the pride and self-centeredness within me, so that I no longer think I can grasp everything but humbly acknowledge my limits and rely on You wholeheartedly. When circumstances change, plans are blocked, and difficulties come, help me not to lose heart or complain but to seek Your will with reverence. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me and the Holy Spirit guide my every step, so that I give thanks in good times and trust in hard times, live out the life of Christ, and give all glory to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: God does great things that I cannot comprehend; I will still fear him humbly and trust him to govern all things!

t: Worship the One True God; Let No Idol Replace God
v: Yahweh spoke to you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the voice of words, but you saw no form; only you heard a voice.
He declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to perform, even the ten commandments; and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
Yahweh commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might do them in the land where you go over to possess it.
Take good heed therefore to yourselves, for you saw no kind of form on the day that Yahweh spoke to you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire,
lest you corrupt yourselves, and make you a engraved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth.

Beware lest you lift up your eyes to the sky, and when you see the sun and the moon and the stars, even all the army of the sky, you be drawn away and worship them, and serve them, which Yahweh your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole sky.
b: Moses reminded the people of Israel that when God spoke to them from the fire at Horeb, they heard only a voice and saw no form. God did not ask the people to know him by any form seen with their eyes, but had them understand his will through the words he revealed. True faith is not shaping a god according to our own imagination, but knowing him according to the truth he has revealed.

People often want God to match their expectations; they like to hear words that comfort them but are unwilling to accept the reminders and corrections of God’s truth. When we use our own ideas to decide what God should be like, it is easy to put our own wishes above God’s will. So we must take the Bible as our standard and let God’s word renew our mindset, no longer knowing God according to our preferences, but humbly obeying the truth he has revealed.

Moses then warned the people not to make any carved image, nor to worship the sun, moon, and stars of the sky. For all of these are created things, and only Yahweh is the true God who created all things. The essence of an idol is putting something created in the place of the Creator, so that the position that belongs to God is taken by something else.

Today we may not carve idols, but we may make money, power, achievement, relationships, or even our own ideas the center of life. When something matters more than God, when our own interests take priority over God’s will, we have already drifted from our rightful place of worshiping the true God. Pride is leaving our rightful place and trying to seize God’s authority; humility is laying down our own sovereignty and returning to our rightful place, letting God be God. When we no longer center on ourselves but let Jesus be King, we turn from a self-centered life to a selfless life, and God once again becomes the one Lord of our lives.

Finally, Moses repeatedly urged the people to be careful, because people are easily drawn by what their eyes see and gradually drift from God. God gave the Ten Commandments, statutes, and ordinances not only so that the people would know what may and may not be done, but so that they would live out a life belonging to God in the promised land. True worship is not only confessing with the mouth that God is Lord, but truly letting God be King in daily life.

When we fix our eyes on Jesus, with him as our example, the Bible as our standard, and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we are no longer pulled by the world’s values; truth changes our mindset, mindset changes our life, and life changes our daily living. True victory is not having everything the world envies, but letting nothing take God’s place, and building God’s divine order in daily life, relationships, and ministry, so that all glory goes to him.
a: Know God through the truth of the Bible
Do not know God according to your imagination and preferences; listen carefully to, understand, and obey God’s word.
Examine the hidden idols in your life
Check whether money, power, achievement, and your own ideas have taken the place that should belong to God.
Let Jesus be King in daily life
Do not only worship God with your mouth; in your daily choices, relationships, and ministry, put God’s will first.
q: In my life, what person, thing, or even idea of my own matters more than God’s will? Am I truly letting Jesus be King, or am I still holding tightly to my own sovereignty?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the one true God who created heaven, earth, and all things. You reveal Your truth through the Bible, so that I can know You, worship You, and obey Your will. Please shine Your light on me so that I can see the hidden idols in my life, and no longer put money, power, achievement, and my own wishes in Your place. I am willing to lay myself down, return to my rightful place as a human being, let You be God, and let Jesus be King in me. Holy Spirit, lead me so that I am not drawn by the world’s values but take the Bible as my standard, obey Your word every day, and live out the life of Christ, so that my daily life, relationships, and ministry all display Your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will keep God’s word, let no idol replace God, worship the one true God all my life, and let Jesus be King!

t: Praise in Affliction; Let God Open the Doors of Life
v: The multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates tore their clothes off of them, and commanded them to be beaten with rods.
When they had laid many stripes on them, they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely;
who, having received such a command, threw them into the inner prison, and secured their feet in the stocks.
But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken. Immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.
The jailer, being roused out of sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!”
He called for lights, sprang in, and fell down trembling before Paul and Silas,
and brought them out and said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”
b: Because they preached the gospel, Paul and Silas were attacked by the crowd, beaten with rods by the magistrates, thrown into the inner prison, and even had their feet fastened in the stocks. They had done no wrong, yet suffered unjust treatment. But at midnight, they did not complain, curse, or feel sorry for themselves; they prayed and sang hymns to God. True faith is not praising God only when circumstances are smooth, but still believing God reigns in the darkest hour.

The old self, meeting unfairness, is easily filled with anger and grievance and focuses on the harm it has suffered; but Paul and Silas turned their focus to God. Their bodies were bound, yet their spirits were not bound by circumstances. When we lay down self-centeredness, no longer let circumstances decide our attitude, and let Jesus be King, we can still have heavenly peace and joy in affliction.

Just as Paul and Silas were praying and praising, a great earthquake suddenly came, the prison doors flew open, and everyone’s bonds were loosened. This was a wonderful work of God, showing that human power can restrain the body but cannot hinder God’s power. The greatest value of prayer and praise is not only changing circumstances but helping us keep trusting and honoring God in them.

Paul and Silas did not wait for the doors to open before they began to praise; they were already worshiping God while the doors were still shut. They did not have faith because they saw a miracle; because they trusted God, they prayed and praised even when they could see no way out. Sometimes God changes our circumstances, and sometimes he lets us experience his sufficient grace within them. When we no longer depend on our own ability but seek the Holy Spirit’s guidance, we can learn to honor the Lord as great in any situation and let affliction become an opportunity to display God’s glory.

What is most moving is that after the doors opened, Paul and Silas did not take the chance to escape, but cried out loudly to protect the jailer’s life: “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!” They did not care only for their own freedom but for the one who had guarded them. True victory is not only that our own chains are loosed, but that we are freed from a self-centered life and are willing to save others with Christ’s love.

The jailer had originally cared only about how to guard prisoners, but through the witness of Paul and Silas’ lives, he began to care about how he himself could be saved. This shows us that the witness of a life can become a bridge for the gospel. Paul and Silas first lived out Christ and then led people to know Christ. When we let Jesus live in us and be King in us, even in affliction we can still be a blessing to others, helping more people know salvation, and all glory goes to God.
a: Keep praising God in affliction
Do not let grievance, difficulty, and circumstances rule your heart; learn to pray, give thanks, and praise God even in the hardest times.
Trust God firmly in hardship
You need not wait until the problem is solved to have faith; believe God still reigns even before you see a way out.
Care for others even when hurt
Seek not only your own release but care for others’ lives with Christ’s love, so that people come to know Jesus through your witness.
q: When I am wronged, hurt, or in difficulty, do I let circumstances rule my emotions, or am I willing, like Paul and Silas, to praise God in affliction and be a blessing to others with Christ’s love?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are the God who governs all things, is full of power, and is full of love. When I face affliction, grievance, and unfair treatment, please keep me from being bound by circumstances and keep anger and complaint from ruling my heart. I am willing to lay myself down and let Jesus be King in me, so that I still pray in difficulty, still praise in darkness, and still trust You when I cannot see the way out. Holy Spirit, lead me so that I care not only about my own needs but also care for others with Christ’s love, and let my life be a witness to the gospel. May more people come to know Jesus and receive salvation through my life and service, and all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will pray and praise God in affliction, trust his great power, live out Christ’s love, and lead people to salvation!

t: Turn Back and Cry Out to God; Turn Defeat into Victory by the Lord
v: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight: and Yahweh strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight.
He gathered the children of Ammon and Amalek to him; and he went and struck Israel, and they possessed the city of palm trees.
The children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

But when the children of Israel cried to Yahweh, Yahweh raised up a savior for them, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. The children of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab.
Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length; and he wore it under his clothing on his right thigh.
He offered the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
When he had finished offering the tribute, he sent away the people who bore the tribute.
But he himself turned back from the quarries that were by Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” The king said, “Keep silence!” All who stood by him left him.
Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you.” He arose out of his seat.
Ehud put out his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body.
The handle also went in after the blade; and the fat closed on the blade, for he didn’t draw the sword out of his body; and it came out behind.
Then Ehud went out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked them.
When he had gone out, his servants came; and they saw, and behold, the doors of the upper room were locked; and they said, “Surely he is covering his feet in the upper room.”
They waited until they were ashamed; and behold, he didn’t open the doors of the upper room; therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the floor.
Ehud escaped while they delayed, and passed beyond the quarries, and escaped to Seirah.
It happened, when he had come, that he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he before them.

He said to them, “Follow me, for Yahweh has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” They went down after him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and didn’t allow any man to pass over.
They struck at that time of Moab about ten thousand men, every strong man, and every man of valor; and not a man escaped.
So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. The land had rest eighty years.
b: The people of Israel again did what was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and as a result were oppressed by Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years. The book of Judges shows a heartbreaking cycle again and again: forsaking God, falling into sin, being oppressed, crying out to God, and being delivered by God. The greatest human failure is not meeting a powerful enemy but leaving God and letting sin reign in life.

Israel was originally God’s chosen and rescued people, but because they were unwilling to obey God, they lost their freedom. We may be the same today: when people insist on their own way and are self-centered, they are easily bound by pride, selfish desires, and sin. True repentance is not only hoping God removes the difficulty, but being willing to leave the wrong path, lay down our own sovereignty, and let God be King again. When we turn from a self-centered life to a selfless life and return to God, we can begin to walk the path of true victory.

When the people of Israel cried out to Yahweh, God raised up a deliverer for them, Ehud. He was a Benjamite, and the Bible specifically records that he was “left-handed,” and God used that very trait to make him an instrument for delivering Israel. God chooses people not because they meet the world’s standards, but because he has his own purpose and can use different people to accomplish his work.

Ehud used courage and strategy, in the warfare of that time, to kill the king of Moab who oppressed Israel and lead the people to freedom. This account is a deliverance event in a specific history; it does not encourage believers today to solve problems by violence, but shows us that God can raise up fitting instruments. What truly matters is not what special ability I have, but whether I am willing to put myself in God’s hands. When we no longer exalt our own talent but humbly obey God, we can become instruments he uses so that his will is accomplished.

After killing the king of Moab, Ehud returned to the people of Israel, blew the trumpet, called the people to follow him, and declared, “Yahweh has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” He did not give the glory of victory to his own courage and strategy, but pointed out that the one who truly brought deliverance was Yahweh. In the end Moab was subdued, and the land had rest for eighty years. True victory is not proving how strong I am, but acknowledging that God is the source of victory and letting all glory go to him.

What Ehud brought was deliverance and peace within that history, but what Jesus Christ brings us is a deeper, eternal salvation, enabling us to be freed from the grip of sin and live a new life. When we let Jesus live in us and be King in us, with the Bible as our standard and the Holy Spirit as our guide, we can turn from the bondage of sin to freedom in Christ, and from a life of failure to one of victory through the Lord, building a life and daily living that belong to God, so that all glory goes to God.
a: Turn from sin and return to God
Do not wait until you are in trouble to think of God; examine your life every day, turn from sin, and let Jesus be King.
Be humble and obedient; become a fitting instrument
Do not shrink back because of your limits, and do not be proud of your ability; be willing to let God use you to accomplish his commission.
Win by the Lord; give glory to God
Do not rely on your own cleverness and ability; trust God’s leading and live out Christ’s victorious life in daily living.
q: Is there still pride, self-centeredness, or disobedience to God in my life that has made me lose spiritual freedom? Am I willing to repent sincerely, let Jesus be King, and turn from failure to victory through him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You that You are full of mercy, hear our cries, and bring deliverance. When I have drifted from Your path because of pride, self-centeredness, and disobedience, please shine Your light on me so that I truly repent and return to You. I am willing to lay myself down and no longer let the selfish desires and sin of the old self be king, but let Jesus live in me and be King in me. Holy Spirit, lead me so that I am humble and obedient and become an instrument You can use, not relying on my own ability but trusting Your great power. May I live out Christ’s victorious life every day, turn from failure to victory, and become a blessing to others, so that all glory goes to You. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I will call on Yahweh, trust his deliverance, obey his leading, and turn defeat into victory by the Lord!
